name: Venice
title: UTM Thickness Gauging in Venice and Porto Marghera
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Venice and Porto Marghera for chemical tankers, bulk carriers and ro-pax ships: ESP gauging and hull structure.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement in Venice and Porto Marghera
intro: Commercial shipping in Venice means Porto Marghera, the industrial port on the mainland edge of the lagoon, reached through the Malamocco inlet. Chemical and product tankers, bulk carriers, general cargo ships and ro-pax ferries at Fusina all work within the lagoon's draught and tidal limits. An Atlantis NDT ultrasonic thickness measurement team travels from India to gauge them at berth, with the work planned around the cargo window and the lagoon's access constraints.

highlights.p: Porto Marghera's petrochemical berths and the Eni biorefinery bring chemical and product tankers that fall under the ESP regime, so chemical tanker thickness gauging of ballast tanks, cofferdams and deck piping is a steady Venice request.

highlights.h: Long stays alongside in the lagoon
highlights.p: Pilotage, tugs and tidal planning for the Malamocco–Marghera channel mean ships rarely make quick calls, which usually leaves a full working day or more at berth to complete a defined gauging scope.

Channel and draught limits keep lagoon traffic to handysize bulk carriers, product and chemical tankers, feeder container ships and ro-pax ferries, which shapes both the survey regimes involved and the size of a typical job.

port.h: The port of Venice: Porto Marghera, Fusina and the lagoon
p: Venice's commercial port is not in the historic city but at Porto Marghera, the industrial zone on the mainland side of the lagoon, together with the passenger terminals of the Marittima and the ro-ro terminal at Fusina. The North Adriatic Sea port system also includes Chioggia at the southern end of the lagoon. Merchant ships enter through the Malamocco inlet and follow the Malamocco–Marghera channel to the industrial basins, where berths serve petroleum products, chemicals, agricultural and other dry bulk, containers and general cargo.

Two features of the lagoon shape inspection here. First, draught and channel limits keep ships smaller than at open-sea Adriatic ports: handysize bulk carriers, product and chemical tankers, feeder container ships and general cargo ships rather than the largest classes. Second, the MOSE mobile barriers, raised at the three lagoon inlets when high tides are forecast, temporarily stop ship movements through the inlets. Port schedules absorb this, but a departure can move by hours, which often gives a gauging team useful extra time alongside and occasionally takes some away, so the plan has to be prioritised. For thickness gauging in Porto Marghera, the practical result is a job sized to a mid-size ship with a full working day alongside.

The cargo mix explains the inspection demand. Porto Marghera's petrochemical and chemical berths, and the Eni biorefinery in the industrial zone, bring chemical and product tankers whose ballast tanks, cofferdams and deck piping need regular gauging, and whose ESP status means renewal surveys from the third onward include extensive measurement of tank structure. Dry bulk berths add hold and topside tank work on bulk carriers once cargo is out. Cruise traffic has changed since 2021, when large cruise ships were barred from St Mark's Basin and the Giudecca Canal; smaller ships still use the passenger terminals, and Fincantieri's Marghera yard continues to build large cruise ships in the industrial zone.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Venice and the lagoon ports
p: Almost all gauging in Venice is done afloat at the commercial berths of Porto Marghera. Tanker berths in the petrochemical area allow deck, piping and ballast tank gauging during cargo operations under the terminal's permit rules, while dry bulk and general cargo quays give access to holds and hatch covers once discharge is complete. Because transits depend on pilotage, tugs and the tide, ships tend to stay alongside for whole working days, and a well-planned job can cover a meaningful part of a survey programme without delaying sailing.

Ro-pax ferries and ro-ro ships use the terminal at Fusina on the mainland edge of the lagoon, and the remaining cruise traffic uses the Marittima terminals. Chioggia, at the southern end of the lagoon, handles smaller general cargo and bulk ships. Large drydockings are often booked at yards elsewhere in the Adriatic or the Mediterranean, and a pre-docking survey in Marghera gives the chosen yard firm steel estimates before the ship sails. Access to every berth runs through the ship's agent, who arranges ISPS passes and the inductions the chemical and petroleum terminals require.
list: Petrochemical and chemical berths, Porto Marghera — gauging of ballast tanks, cofferdams, main deck and cargo and ballast piping on chemical and product tankers during cargo operations
Dry bulk quays, Porto Marghera — after discharge of agricultural or other dry bulk cargo, hold frames, topside tanks, hatch covers and coamings on handysize bulk carriers
Container and multipurpose terminals, Porto Marghera — readings on feeder and multipurpose ships, mainly ballast tanks, hatch covers and the scrubber discharge line where fitted
Fusina ro-ro terminal — vehicle deck, ramp and ballast tank gauging on ro-pax and ro-ro ships while they lie alongside between sailings
Marittima passenger terminals — the smaller cruise ships that still call, gauged during turnaround on their scrubber lines and items carried over from the last survey
Chioggia — gauging on smaller general cargo and bulk ships at the southern lagoon port, combined with Marghera work in a single mobilisation

context.h: Regulation, emissions and market context in the Venice lagoon
p: Port state control at Marghera and Chioggia is carried out by the Italian Coast Guard under the Paris MoU. Chemical tankers are surveyed under IACS UR Z10.3 and product tankers under Z10.1 or Z10.4, and for these ESP ships the third renewal survey and those after it bring extensive gauging of cargo and ballast tank structure. Chemical tankers often have stainless steel cargo tanks that change little over a ship's life, while the mild-steel ballast tanks, cofferdams and deck structure carry the corrosion; the gauging effort follows the steel, not the tank count.

Ships crossing the lagoon inlets have sailed within the Mediterranean SOx ECA from its start date of 1 May 2025, which means 0.10% sulphur fuel or a scrubber meeting the same emission limit. Rules on open-loop wash-water discharge differ between ports and coastal states, so masters confirm local requirements through the agent before arrival, and scrubber overboard piping benefits from regular wall-thickness checks whatever mode the system runs in. EU ETS, applying to shipping since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime, since 2025, bear on older handysize bulk carriers and product tankers, where the decision to keep, sell or recycle a ship often turns on the condition of its steel.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Venice and Porto Marghera
jobs.p: Venice jobs are almost always at berth in Porto Marghera, with the ship working cargo. The lagoon's pilotage and tidal planning usually mean the ship stays alongside for a full working day or more, so the team can cover a defined block of tanks and decks with time to re-measure anything doubtful. Scope, permits and the reporting format are fixed with the superintendent before anyone travels from India.
list: ESP thickness measurement of a chemical tanker's ballast tanks and cofferdams at a Marghera chemical berth, ahead of its third renewal survey
Hold and topside tank gauging on a handysize bulk carrier after grain discharge, closing out substantial corrosion items noted at the last annual survey
Vehicle deck and stern ramp gauging on a ro-pax ferry at Fusina, completed in the hours between arrival and the next departure
Pre-docking gauging of a product tanker's main deck and ballast tanks at Marghera, so the repair yard can plan steel renewal before the ship sails
Scrubber overboard pipe wall-thickness survey on a feeder container ship at a Marghera terminal, repeated on later calls to trend the rate of loss

logistics: Venice Marco Polo Airport is on the mainland edge of the lagoon, close to Porto Marghera, and Treviso airport adds further European connections. Porto Marghera is reached by road rather than by water, which makes equipment handling simpler than anywhere in the historic city. The ship's agent arranges ISPS access and terminal inductions for the chemical and petroleum berths, which apply their own safety rules. Travel for our Indian technicians is on Schengen visas, and we fix flights once the ship's lagoon transit is confirmed, since tides and barrier closures can shift arrival times.

faqs.q: Do MOSE barrier closures affect a gauging job in Porto Marghera?
faqs.a: They can affect the ship's arrival and departure, not the gauging itself. When the barriers are raised at the lagoon inlets, transits pause until they are lowered again. A delayed departure usually gives extra time alongside; a delayed arrival can compress the window. We keep the scope prioritised so that the most important spaces are measured first whatever happens to the schedule.

faqs.q: Can you gauge stainless steel cargo tanks on a chemical tanker?
faqs.a: Yes. Ultrasonic gauges measure stainless steel once calibrated for it, although stainless cargo tanks rarely show significant wastage. The structure that usually needs attention on a chemical tanker is the mild-steel ballast tanks, cofferdams, deck plating and piping. We plan readings to meet the class requirements for the ship's survey and put the effort where corrosion is likely.

faqs.q: Is hull gauging in Venice possible on cruise ships after the 2021 restrictions?
faqs.a: Yes, on the ships that still call. Large cruise ships no longer pass through St Mark's Basin and the Giudecca Canal, but smaller ships continue to use the passenger terminals. Gauging on them is done during turnaround and usually targets scrubber piping, void spaces and items carried over from the previous survey.

faqs.q: Where do ships from Venice go for drydock gauging?
faqs.a: Wherever the owner books the docking, often a yard elsewhere in the Adriatic or the Mediterranean. We can gauge the ship in Marghera beforehand to give the yard steel estimates, then mobilise the same team to the yard for the full programme, so the readings stay consistent from first estimate to final report.
